# Probably Proven: Ziyad Hanna on Formal Verification and AI | Wearing Flip-Flops


24 Nov 2026


• 2 minute read


-
-
-
-


Formal verification gives you a mathematical yes or no. A large language model gives you its best guess. Put the two together, and you get either the most trustworthy AI in chip design, or a very convincing green checkmark.


In episode 14 of[Wearing Flip-Flops](https://wearing-flip-flops.com/) , the semiconductor podcast for chip designers, Ziyad Hanna, Corporate Vice President of R&D and Strategic Head of AI at Cadence, returns for a second conversation with host Ronen Laviv, this time on formal verification, AI, and the cloud.


## Why Formal Anchors Agentic AI


Formal has been central to Cadence since Jasper joined us in 2014, and Ziyad led Jasper R&D before taking on AI strategy. That history shapes how we build agents: an AI agent is only as good as the engines underneath it.


The ChipStack AI Super Agent, now at Level-5 autonomy, runs formal analysis as part of its own loop, driving Jasper Formal Verification alongside Xcelium Logic Simulation and iterating toward closure rather than waiting for step-by-step prompts. Grounding every agent action in signoff-accurate engines is what turns autonomy into something a design team can trust.


That gives formal verification a new role. It is no longer only a specialist’s tool for control logic and protocols. In an agentic flow, it becomes the referee that keeps a probabilistic model honest.


## The Questions Engineers Are Asking


Ronen spent 14 of his 25 years in semiconductors at Cadence, and he brought the questions verification teams are asking right now:


- When did formal verification cross from research into everyday engineering work?
- Is an LLM in front of a formal engine a category error, or the thing that makes AI safe to use?
- When AI writes the assertions, how do you catch weak or vacuous properties that prove trivially and still show green?
- Does AI make bounded proofs more trustworthy, or just more comfortable?
- State space explosion and the formal skills barrier: what AI solves, and what it might hide
- Formal apps, AI agents, and how many engineers can now drive Jasper on their own
- Where the line between formal and simulation sits in 2026
- When agents launch hundreds of simulation and formal jobs, who schedules them, and how compute and licensing scale in the cloud


The title, Probably Proven, is the whole debate in two words. Where Ziyad lands on it is in the episode.
